title: 05 — Unity Catalog in Depth
html:
05 — Unity Catalog in Depth

The one idea: Unity Catalog is the one place where every data and AI object has a name, an owner, permissions, lineage and an audit trail. Engines ask it for permission and for credentials. Get the object model and the privilege rules right, and governance becomes configuration instead of code.

1. What it is

Unity Catalog (UC) is the Databricks governance layer. It is also an open-source project, but this chapter describes the Databricks service. The Databricks platform chapter introduces the three-level namespace and grants. This chapter covers the full object model, table types, storage access, fine-grained access, ABAC, lineage and system tables.

SQL Server comparison: UC is like a server-level catalog spanning every database, with logins, schemas and permissions, plus built-in auditing and lineage. It governs files in cloud storage, not pages inside one server.

2. Why it matters

  • Rights at delivery, masks and row filters all depend on UC being the single enforcement point.
  • Open access: UC serves the Iceberg REST endpoint and Delta Sharing, so outside engines get governed access.
  • Audit and cost: system tables answer "who read this", "where did this column come from" and "what did this job cost" with SQL.

3. The main ideas

3.1 The object model

---
title: Unity Catalog — securable objects
---
flowchart TD
    MS["Metastore (one per region)"] --> CAT["Catalog"]
    MS --> SC["Storage credential"]
    MS --> EL["External location"]
    MS --> CONN["Connection (for federation)"]
    MS --> SH["Share / Recipient / Provider"]
    CAT --> SCH["Schema"]
    SCH --> T["Table (managed, external, foreign)"]
    SCH --> V["View / metric view / materialized view"]
    SCH --> VOL["Volume (managed or external)"]
    SCH --> FN["Function (UDF, row filter, mask)"]
    SCH --> MOD["Registered model"]
Object What it is
Catalog, schema Namespaces: catalog.schema.object
Managed table UC owns the storage location and lifecycle. Eligible for predictive optimization. Can be Delta or (GA per Databricks) Iceberg
External table Data in a path you manage. UC governs access, but you own the files' lifecycle
Foreign table Metadata owned by another catalog (federation, or foreign Iceberg such as Glue). UC governs reads
Volume Governed non-tabular files (PDFs, images, raw drops) under /Volumes/catalog/schema/volume/
Storage credential, external location How UC reaches cloud storage (for example, an Azure managed identity) and which paths it may use
Function SQL or Python UDFs, including row-filter and mask functions
Registered model MLflow models governed in UC (catalog.schema.model)
Metric view Business measures and dimensions defined once (see 07)

3.2 Privileges and inheritance

  • Grants on a catalog or schema are inherited by everything below it.
  • To touch a table you also need USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA on its parents. SELECT alone is not enough.
  • Common privileges: SELECT, MODIFY, CREATE TABLE, READ VOLUME, WRITE VOLUME, EXECUTE, ALL PRIVILEGES, MANAGE.
  • Owners can grant on their objects. Assign ownership to groups, not people.
  • Grant to groups (synced from Microsoft Entra ID), never to individuals.

3.3 Fine-grained access: three options

Option Scope When
Dynamic views One view Simple, older pattern
Row filters and column masks on a table One table, with a function attached by ALTER TABLE ... SET ROW FILTER or ALTER COLUMN ... SET MASK A few sensitive tables
ABAC policies with governed tags Every table whose columns carry a tag, across a catalog or schema Many tables, for example "mask every column tagged pii.pan"

Status, checked 2026-10-26: Databricks announced ABAC row-filter and column-mask policies, governed tags and automated data classification as generally available. The release notes list governed tags as GA on 2 April 2026, and the blog and community posts date the combined announcement to May 2026.

3.4 Lineage and system tables

UC captures table and column lineage automatically for workloads that run on Databricks. System tables expose it, together with audit and billing. Some tables were labelled Public Preview in some doc versions, so check for your workspace.

System table Answers
system.access.audit Who did what, when (365-day retention)
system.access.table_lineage, system.access.column_lineage Which job read or wrote which table and column
system.billing.usage, system.billing.list_prices What each job, warehouse or endpoint cost
system.lakeflow.jobs, job_tasks, job_run_timeline, job_task_run_timeline Every job, task and run with timings

3.5 Open access

  • Iceberg REST endpoint: outside engines read UC tables as Iceberg, with credentials vended per request (see 03).
  • Delta Sharing: governed sharing to other organisations and platforms (see 08).

4. Working code

The script models three UC rules: inheritance, the USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA requirement, and group membership. Standard library only.

# Unity Catalog privilege rules in miniature:
# 1. Privileges granted on a catalog or schema are inherited by everything below it.
# 2. To reach a table you also need USE CATALOG on its catalog and USE SCHEMA on its schema.
# 3. Groups: a user gets what their groups get.
grants = {
    ("catalog", "fin"):                   {"data_readers": {"USE CATALOG"}},
    ("schema", "fin.gold"):               {"data_readers": {"USE SCHEMA", "SELECT"}},
    ("schema", "fin.silver"):             {"engineers": {"USE SCHEMA", "SELECT", "MODIFY"}},
    ("table", "fin.silver.fund_nav"):     {"data_readers": {"SELECT"}},
}
groups = {"asha": {"data_readers"}, "ravi": {"engineers"}, "meera": {"data_readers", "engineers"}}

def privileges_on(user, kind, name):
    out = set()
    for g in groups.get(user, set()) | {user}:
        out |= grants.get((kind, name), {}).get(g, set())
    return out

def can(user, privilege, table):
    catalog, schema, _ = table.split(".")
    if "USE CATALOG" not in privileges_on(user, "catalog", catalog):
        return False, f"no USE CATALOG on {catalog}"
    if "USE SCHEMA" not in privileges_on(user, "schema", f"{catalog}.{schema}"):
        return False, f"no USE SCHEMA on {catalog}.{schema}"
    inherited = (privileges_on(user, "catalog", catalog) | privileges_on(user, "schema", f"{catalog}.{schema}")
                 | privileges_on(user, "table", table))
    return (privilege in inherited), ("ok" if privilege in inherited else f"no {privilege} on {table} or its parents")

checks = [("asha", "SELECT", "fin.gold.fund_metrics"),
          ("asha", "SELECT", "fin.silver.fund_nav"),
          ("ravi", "SELECT", "fin.silver.fund_nav"),
          ("meera", "MODIFY", "fin.silver.fund_nav"),
          ("asha", "MODIFY", "fin.gold.fund_metrics")]
for user, priv, table in checks:
    print(f"{user:6s} {priv:7s} {table:22s} -> {can(user, priv, table)}")

Output:

asha   SELECT  fin.gold.fund_metrics  -> (True, 'ok')
asha   SELECT  fin.silver.fund_nav    -> (False, 'no USE SCHEMA on fin.silver')
ravi   SELECT  fin.silver.fund_nav    -> (False, 'no USE CATALOG on fin')
meera  MODIFY  fin.silver.fund_nav    -> (True, 'ok')
asha   MODIFY  fin.gold.fund_metrics  -> (False, 'no MODIFY on fin.gold.fund_metrics or its parents')

What to notice:

  • asha has SELECT granted directly on fin.silver.fund_nav, but still can't read it, because her group lacks USE SCHEMA on fin.silver. This is the most common "permission denied" puzzle in UC.
  • ravi has everything on the schema but no USE CATALOG, so he can't reach it.
  • meera combines both groups' grants.

The real SQL, not run here:

-- Not run: requires a Unity Catalog workspace.
GRANT USE CATALOG ON CATALOG fin TO `data_readers`;
GRANT USE SCHEMA, SELECT ON SCHEMA fin.gold TO `data_readers`;

CREATE FUNCTION fin.gov.mask_pan(pan STRING)
RETURN CASE WHEN is_account_group_member('kyc_readers') THEN pan ELSE concat('XXXXX', right(pan, 5)) END;
ALTER TABLE fin.silver.issuers ALTER COLUMN pan SET MASK fin.gov.mask_pan;

SELECT event_time, user_identity.email, action_name, request_params
FROM system.access.audit
WHERE action_name = 'getTable' AND event_date >= current_date() - INTERVAL 7 DAYS;

5. Common mistakes

  1. Granting SELECT without USE SCHEMA and USE CATALOG. Access is denied, and nobody understands why.
  2. Granting to individuals. People move teams and grants rot. Use Entra ID groups.
  3. External tables by default. You lose predictive optimization and lifecycle management. Prefer managed tables unless another system must own the files.
  4. Raw files outside volumes. Ungoverned paths escape audit and lineage. Land files in volumes.
  5. Per-table masks on hundreds of tables. Use governed tags and ABAC policies.

6. Exercise (1.5 hours)

  1. Extend the script with ownership: an owner can grant on their object without any explicit privilege.
  2. Add ABAC: columns carry tags, and a policy masks every column tagged pii unless the user is in kyc_readers.
  3. On Databricks Free Edition, create a catalog, schema, volume and table, grant SELECT to a group, then query system.access.audit for your own actions, if your workspace exposes it.

7. Questions to test yourself

  1. What three privileges does a reader need to SELECT from fin.gold.t?
  2. What is the difference between managed, external and foreign tables?
  3. When would you pick ABAC over a per-table row filter?
  4. Which system table shows column-level lineage?
  5. Where should raw PDFs live in UC, and why?

Answers

  1. USE CATALOG on fin, USE SCHEMA on fin.gold, and SELECT on the table or one of its parents.
  2. Managed: UC owns the storage and lifecycle. External: UC governs access to files you own. Foreign: another catalog owns the metadata, and UC governs reads.
  3. When the same rule applies to many tables. Tag the columns once, and one policy covers them all.
  4. system.access.column_lineage.
  5. In a volume, so every read and write is governed, audited and visible in lineage.
